summary: A segmented date field with a calendar attached, taking and returning a YYYY-MM-DD string.
useWhen: the user picks one calendar date — an event date, a due date, a birthday
the date has to be typed as well as clicked, because the user often already knows it
some dates must be refused individually rather than as a continuous range

useInstead.when: the user picks a start and an end
useInstead.why: two DatePickers cannot stop the end preceding the start, cannot show the days between them, and give the user two calendars to reconcile from memory

useInstead.when: the value is a month or a year rather than a day
useInstead.why: a calendar grid to choose 'March' is twelve options rendered as thirty-one

useInstead.when: the field is one of a short, known set of dates the product defines
useInstead.why: picking from four delivery slots is a choice from a list, not a date

useInstead.when: a time of day is part of the value
useInstead.why: this picker is fixed to day granularity; put a TimeField beside it — the two share one box and one set of states

guarantees: each editable segment is its own tab stop, as in Chrome's native <input type=date>; the locale's separators are not, and arrow keys move between segments as well, so neither convention has to be learned
the segments sit in one labelled group, so the field's name is announced once on entry rather than repeated per segment
each segment announces its own name, value and bounds, so 'month, 4, minimum 1, maximum 12' is heard rather than an opaque number
field order and separators come from Intl, so a German reader edits DD.MM.YYYY and a US reader MM/DD/YYYY from the same component and the same value
the calendar overlay is modal: focus moves into the grid, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive tech, Escape closes it and focus returns to the field
every day cell carries the full date as its accessible name in the reader's own language, so the narrow weekday headers are never load-bearing
unavailable and disabled days are distinguished visually and in the accessible name, not by colour alone
today is marked with a dot rather than a ring, so it cannot be mistaken for a second selected day
the selected fill and the segment focus box are redeclared under forced-colors, where background-color is discarded
requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
`calendarLabel` wording if 'Open calendar' is wrong for the context — it is the button's whole accessible name

antiPatterns.dont: passing a Date object, a timestamp, or a locale-formatted string as `value`
antiPatterns.why: the value is a calendar date with no time and no zone, spelled YYYY-MM-DD. `new Date('2026-04-12')` parses as UTC midnight and displays as the 11th for every reader west of Greenwich. A malformed value throws with the prop name rather than rendering an empty field

antiPatterns.dont: using `isDateUnavailable` to express a lower or upper bound
antiPatterns.why: `minValue` and `maxValue` also disable the navigation arrows past the bound, so the user cannot page into a month with nothing selectable in it. A predicate is for the holes inside the bounds

antiPatterns.dont: hiding the field and leaving only the calendar button
antiPatterns.why: typing a date is faster than clicking one for anyone who already knows it, and paging a calendar back to a birth year is the worst interaction in any form

antiPatterns.dont: styling a day cell with :hover for the keyboard highlight
antiPatterns.why: use [data-selected], [data-today], [data-disabled] and [data-unavailable]. Pointer hover and keyboard focus are different states here and a grid where they disagree has two apparent cursors

antiPatterns.dont: reading the posted form value from the segments
antiPatterns.why: they are spinbuttons with no name. Pass `name` and the component posts the ISO value in a hidden input
the group is a set of spinbuttons rather than one form control, so there is nothing for htmlFor to point at. Pass `label` and react-aria wires the name through aria-labelledby

antiPatterns.dont: adding a roving tabindex so the field becomes one tab stop
antiPatterns.why: it buys back two tabs per field and costs the ability to Tab straight to the year, which is the segment users most often fix on its own. It also diverges from the native date input, which is the convention they already have

label.expects: what the date is for — 'Event starts', not 'Date'

description.expects: helper text under the field; replaced by `errorMessage` when `isInvalid`

errorMessage.expects: what is wrong and what would be right, shown only when `isInvalid`
